Rank fitted models by AIC, AICc, or BIC

Source: R/aic_table.R
aic_table.Rd

Creates a model-selection table from fitted terradish models using AIC, AICc, or BIC.

Usage

aic_table(
  mod_list,
  AICc = FALSE,
  BIC = FALSE,
  mod_names = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

mod_list

List of fitted terradish models.

AICc

Should second-order AIC (Akaike's information criterion with small-sample correction) be used instead of AIC? When TRUE, the correction uses \(n\) = number of focal sampling sites (not the number of pairwise observations). A common guideline is to prefer AICc over AIC when \(n / K < 40\), where \(K\) is the number of estimated parameters.

BIC

Should BIC be used instead of AIC? When TRUE, the penalty uses \(n\) = number of focal sampling sites (individuals or populations), the same sample size as AICc, not the number of pairwise observations. Pairs that share a site are not independent, so the number of pairs overstates the information in the data.

mod_names

Optional model names. By default the right-hand side of each fitted formula is used. For MLPE measurement models with additional pairwise covariates, the default appends [mlpe:n], where n is the number of added pairwise covariate columns.

verbose

Should the table be printed to the console?

Value

A data frame with one row per model, sorted from best to worst: model (the label), K (number of estimated parameters, conductance plus nuisance), the criterion (AIC, AICc, or BIC; smaller is better), its difference from the best model (Delta_AIC and so on), the model weight and cumulative weight, and loglik. The converged column is true only when both the outer optimizer and final nuisance optimization record code 0. Missing convergence diagnostics in older objects are treated as unverified (false); boundary marks active parameter bounds or no resistance structure. A warning identifies tables containing nonconverged or boundary fits.

Details

At nominal Wishart information, information criteria can favor extensions that are unsupported across replicate histories. Use terradish_cv_folds to select conductance terms and terradish_rescale_nu to assess inferential sensitivity.

Information-criterion comparison requires the same observed response, focal sites, graph domain, and likelihood family. Wishart fits must also use the same effective degrees of freedom, nu. leastsquares and mlpe are Gaussian likelihoods for the same pairwise-distance response and can be ranked when those conditions hold. generalized_wishart and wishart_covariance use different response representations and must not be ranked together. Cross-family rankings, such as mlpe versus generalized_wishart, are invalid.

The function checks response values, model family, fitted dimensions, recorded nu, and retained graph signatures. Older fits without signatures require the user to verify the graph domain.

Worked example

See vignette("v04-model-comparison", package = "terradish") for compatible model rankings, coefficient plots, and predictive comparisons.

See also

terradish_cv_folds for predictive comparison, terradish_rescale_nu for sensitivity to nu, and anova() for nested likelihood-ratio tests.

Other inference and model comparison: mlpe_response_change(), terradish_cv_folds(), terradish_folds(), terradish_ibe_ratio(), terradish_inference, terradish_rescale_nu()

Examples

# \donttest{
library(terra)
#> terra 1.9.34

data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale.
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
coords <- coords[keep]
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords)

fit1 <- terradish(Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, surface,
                  measurement_model = mlpe)
fit2 <- terradish(Fst ~ altitude * forestcover, surface,
                  measurement_model = mlpe)

# One row per model, best first. K counts conductance plus nuisance
# parameters; Delta_AIC is the difference from the best model.
aic_table(list(fit1, fit2))
#>                                           model K       AIC Delta_AIC AIC_wt
#> 2 altitude + forestcover + altitude:forestcover 7 -3007.215    0.0000      1
#> 1                        altitude + forestcover 6 -2978.092   29.1238      0
#>   Cum.wt   loglik converged boundary
#> 2      1 1510.608      TRUE    FALSE
#> 1      1 1495.046      TRUE    FALSE
aic_table(list(fit1, fit2), AICc = TRUE)
#>                                           model K       AIC      AICc
#> 2 altitude + forestcover + altitude:forestcover 7 -3007.215 -3002.346
#> 1                        altitude + forestcover 6 -2978.092 -2974.592
#>   Delta_AICc AICc_wt Cum.wt   loglik converged boundary
#> 2     0.0000       1      1 1510.608      TRUE    FALSE
#> 1    27.7542       0      1 1495.046      TRUE    FALSE
# }
